input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 40. the team planned Kxg3 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Ke3 instead, and that move was played, costing 204 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 2. the team planned a4 (pawn_a2), but pawn_a2 (amnesia) sent a3 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.
- On move 9. the team planned h4 (pawn_h2), but pawn_h2 (amnesia) sent h3 instead, and that move was played, costing 4 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the latest team plan in chat and send only your piece's move if it is the planned move and exactly the planned destination square; if the plan names a different piece, stay silent, and never move because of a threat or an available capture unless the plan says so.
- Before sending, copy the planned move's piece and destination square from the latest plan in chat and check that your move matches it character for character (for a pawn, the same file and the same rank, so h4 is not h3); if it differs in any way, or the plan names another piece, send nothing, whatever the threats or captures on the board.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, write in chat the planned move's piece and exact destination square next to the move you are about to send, and send it only if the two are identical, and if you are the planned piece, send exactly that destination and never a different square even if it looks similar or safer.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
